Be careful with this. Copper is covered by legislation that doesn't cover fiber. The laws haven't caught up and copper is still covered under the various communication acts and is usually overseen by your State PUC. Cable isn't considered a necessary good and service, nor is fiber.

For example, you may not be aware that your State quite likely has laws that allow you to use any DSL provider who is willing to provide the service. The owner of the lines must allow them reasonable access - so that you're not locked into having a specific phone monopoly provider. This also works for DSL, as the same laws govern it.

Cable? Yeah... Try to get your cable (or fiber) provider to allow someone else to provision the service on those same lines. The laws don't govern them as they aren't a quasi-public good that is considered necessary per the current regulations. In time, this is likely to change. For now, that's how it is in every State that I know of - with some exceptions for manicipal systems that are pretty localized.

I have fiber due to run by the main road, sometime this year. For this, and reliability, I'm unlikely to switch.

When you hear talks of ripping out copper and replacing it entirely with fiber, be wary. Check your local laws, before deciding if you think this is a good idea or not.
